title: Iambic Submits IND for a Potentially Brain-Penetrant KIF18A Inhibitor IAM217, Its Second Wholly Owned AI-Discovered Candidate
source_used: Iambic Therapeutics' own press release on iambic.ai (same text as the Business Wire release, which is blocked here)
key_facts: San Diego, 5 Oct 2026: Iambic Therapeutics, a clinical-stage company that develops medicines with an AI-driven platform, announced it has submitted an Investigational New Drug (IND) application to the US FDA to start a Phase 1/2 trial of IAM217, a brain-penetrant inhibitor of KIF18A, for triple-negative breast cancer, ovarian cancer and other solid tumors with chromosomal instability.
In a preclinical brain metastasis model, IAM217 produced approximately 90% regression of established intracranial tumors; the company says it is believed to be brain penetrant.

KIF18A is a protein that governs chromosome alignment during cell division; the company says cancer cells with chromosomal instability depend on it while normal cells tolerate its inhibition, and that emerging clinical evidence potentially validates it as a target in high-grade serous ovarian cancer.

Iambic says its AI platform designed IAM217 without an experimental structure of KIF18A bound to an inhibitor, using NeuralPLexer for structural insight and Enchant for property prediction; brain penetrance was reached within about six months at lead identification.

Subject to FDA clearance of the IND, IAM217 will be Iambic's second program to enter clinical trials; its HER2 inhibitor IAM1363 is in a Phase 1/1b trial and an IND for the CDK2/4 inhibitor IAM-C1 is expected later in Q4 2026.
Every claim is the company's own; the release carries a forward-looking-statements warning.

why_it_matters_hint: An AI-designed cancer drug candidate moves toward human trials, but all evidence so far is the company's own preclinical data and the FDA has not yet cleared the trial.
